# 1.32.0: Work with many chats at once, a sidebar that no longer freezes

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are.

## Many chats at once

- **Select chats with a frame.** Press the mouse on empty space in the chat list, or on a group
  label such as *Folders*, and drag: an accent-coloured frame selects every chat it touches.
  A folder or archive header inside the frame selects all of its chats, even when the folder is
  collapsed. Hold Ctrl to add to the current selection. Pressing on a chat still drags that chat,
  as before. A click on empty space in the list clears the selection, and so does a click
  anywhere else in the window: in the conversation, in the input box, on the sidebar's buttons.
- **Ctrl+A** selects every chat, folder and the archive while the chat list or the conversation
  has the focus. In a text field with text, and inside a code block, it selects the text as
  usual; in Settings and other dialogs it does nothing.
- **Shift+Del** deletes the selected chats, or the open chat when nothing is selected. It asks
  first, as deleting always did. With text selected in a field, it cuts the text instead.
  Both shortcuts can be reassigned in *Settings → General → Keyboard shortcuts*.
- **Right-click** opens a chat's menu, the same one as its ⋯ button. When several chats are
  selected, the menu acts on all of them: rename, pin or unpin, move to a folder, tags, archive or
  restore, share, export and delete. Deleting a selection that includes whole folders deletes
  those folders too.
- **The strip of buttons above the list is gone.** It appeared over the chat list whenever
  something was selected and pushed the list down; everything it did is in the right-click menu.
  From the keyboard, the Menu key (or Shift+F10) opens the same menu for the selection.
- **Share** puts all the selected chats into one code. Codes for several chats start with
  `AMRN2:` and need 1.32.0 or later to open; a code for a single chat is the same as before.
- **Export** to Markdown, HTML or JSON writes one file per chat into a folder you choose. PDF and
  print make a single document, with each chat starting on a new page.
- Deleting hundreds of chats at once now writes the chat index and the folder layout once, not
  once per chat.

## Keys & spending

- **Each key has one menu: Edit, Send, Delete.** It opens with a right-click on the key or with
  the ⋯ button that appears on hover; the separate edit and delete buttons are gone.
- **Send** copies the key to another profile on this computer. No password is asked: a profile
  password only locks the window, and every profile's keys are encrypted for the same Windows
  user. If that profile already has the key, nothing changes, and the profile keeps its own
  active key. Keys from environment variables are already available to every profile and are
  not sent.
- **The warning about an approaching spending limit now reaches you.** It appears right after
  the request that crossed the threshold, not one request later, and it stays under the input
  box for 12 seconds instead of disappearing as soon as the reply ends. Raising a limit lets it
  warn again for the new amount, and switching profiles no longer silences a warning that
  belongs to the other profile.

## Faster

- **Resizing the sidebar no longer freezes the window.** Each step of dragging the sidebar edge
  used to lay out every built message of the open chat again. Now, as with resizing the window,
  only the messages on screen follow the new width during the drag, and the rest catch up in the
  background without moving the place you are reading. On a chat with 1200 messages, a drag step
  went from about 1.5 s to about 20 ms, the longest pause from 0.9 s to about 0.1 s, and
  collapsing or expanding the sidebar (Ctrl+B) from about 1.5 s and 1.0 s to 30-40 ms. Startup
  time is the same as in 1.31.0.
- **Update downloads no longer crawl.** A download that started on a slow or stuck connection
  could take a very long time, while cancelling and pressing Update again finished in seconds.
  Now the download watches its own speed: if nothing arrives for 20 seconds, or less than about
  128 KB/s arrives for 10 seconds, it opens a new connection and continues from the byte it has
  already received, up to four times. A connection timeout is no longer mistaken for you
  pressing Cancel.

## Auto picks the strong model for your safety

- When a message is about the safety of the user or of this computer (something suspicious on
  the machine, accounts or data in someone else's hands, someone trying to deceive you, or how
  to protect against any of it), **Auto answers with the heavy chat model**, even when the work
  itself goes to an agent. The agent's own level is still chosen by the agent router: a scan can
  run on a light model while the strong model reads the results and decides what to do next.

## Fixes

- **Code blocks no longer pull the conversation away.** Clicking or selecting text in a code
  block whose top was scrolled out of view moved the conversation up to the start of the answer,
  right under the mouse, so the selection grew upward through the whole block; a click to the
  right of the code lines jumped to the end of the block. Now the conversation stays where it is,
  and dragging a selection past the edge still scrolls it along.
- **No more accent frame around the input box.** It appeared whenever focus reached the box from
  the keyboard, for example with a space typed while the chat list had focus. Text fields show
  focus with their caret; buttons and switches keep the frame for keyboard navigation.

## Clearer text

- All interface text in Russian and English was reread and rewritten where it was hard to
  follow: shorter sentences, plain words, the same term for the same thing. Long dashes are
  replaced with plain hyphens or a better sentence.
- In the Russian interface, the *New Chat* button and the **+** menu next to the input box are
  now in Russian too. *New language* stays in English, so that someone who does not read
  Russian can find it.
- **Translations made with New language** are told to write plain, exact text without long
  dashes, and any dash that slips through is replaced. Translations you already have get the
  same treatment when they load, except for the lines you corrected by hand.
- The README was rewritten in plainer English.
